rtl.scope: S4DI v1, rank 0, last-value hold, relations on or off (relation program loaded out of band). rank > 0 or predictor zero / linear -> unsupported (rejected at the header); zero / linear temporal-only streams stay on scp4d_tdec (v0.1.11, unchanged). A relation target may not also be a source.

cycle_model: cycles = bytes + max(0, D − header_tail_bytes) + fan_out + [relations] (4·T + nT + Σ_{t≥1} dirty_targets(t)) + 5; fan_out = Σ over non-target source events of the source's fan-out entries (full-rate input; counted from the first cycle after reset to done, inclusive)

break_even.label: LABELLED ESTIMATES (not measurements): bytes and cycles are measured; energy prices are the v0.1.10 45 nm model table (Horowitz ISSCC 2014 + labelled assumptions).
break_even.break_even_byte_cost_note: If energy per decoder cycle is E_c, relations save energy only when moving one stream byte costs more than this many E_c (measured cycles and bytes; E_c itself is not measured).

projection.label: PROJECTION, NOT MEASURED: a variant with the fan-out handled in parallel (4 ACC banks, one source event per cycle) would remove the per-entry stall; cycles = measured − fan_out + source_events.

verdict.answer: DEPENDS on where the stream lives
verdict.decoder_bound: NOT worth it inside the decoder: relations cut the stream 1.836× (T64) but cost 1.8384× the measured cycles (0.7976 vs 0.4339 cycles/element-frame); 48.2% of the relations cycles are fan-out accumulator updates (one per cycle), plus the per-frame dirty-target flush.
verdict.link_or_memory_bound: WORTH it when moving stream bytes is the cost: below ~28.6536 MB/s of link bandwidth (ECP5 fmax estimates) the relations decoder finishes first, and with bytes priced above ~102.2046 pJ/B (DRAM-class 162.5–325 pJ/B in the model table) it is the lower-energy path; with on-chip SRAM pricing (1.25–2.5 pJ/B) it is not.
verdict.area: Relations need the program memories (order, fan-out, accumulators, dirty list) and an 18×32 multiplier: see area (estimates).
